name: cavemio-terms
title: Terms
description: A terms-of-service step with an owl who reads along: Skim sums up each section in one plain line, gets dizzy if you scroll too fast, and gives a thumbs up at the end.

cavemio.accessibility:
- The terms are a focusable, labelled region you can scroll with the keyboard; the bubble is a polite live region, so each section’s summary is read out as you reach it.
- Skim is decoration (aria-hidden) and animated: reading, the yawn, the dizzy wobble and the thumbs up are frames cut from generated animations of his own art, shipped inside skim-art.ts as WebP strips (174KB), so the install is complete. Each pose is one Web Animation of its strip (the yawn plays once); no frame loop.
- Scroll handling writes the reading line straight to the element and only re-renders when the section, the pose or the read state changes.
- With reduced motion each pose shows its first frame, lines swap in place and Skip to the end jumps instead of scrolling.
- Built from Status button, which the CLI installs with it. No animation library.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: sections
props.description: – · { id, title, body, tldr }: body is any React content, tldr is Skim’s one line.

props.name: version
props.description: – · Which terms these are; onAccept gets it back.

props.name: onAccept
props.description: – · Record the acceptance. Throw to say it didn’t save.

props.name: requireRead
props.description: true · Accept stays off until the terms have been scrolled to the end.

props.name: updated / title / name
props.description: — / "Terms of Service" / "Skim" · The line under the title, the title, and the owl’s name in his lines.

features.title: Every section, in a line
features.description: Each section carries a tldr that Skim says as you reach it.

features.title: Read before accepting
features.description: Accept stays off until the pane has been scrolled to the end (requireRead), with Skip to the end for people who know.

features.title: A reading line
features.description: A thin line along the foot of the pane fills as you scroll, written straight to the element.

features.title: The version agreed
features.description: onAccept gets the version string, so you can record exactly which terms were accepted.

features.title: Your own text
features.description: Section bodies are any React content: paragraphs, lists, links.

features.title: Not now
features.description: onDecline shows a second button beside Accept.

states.title: reading
states.description: Skim sits bottom left of the lit stage with his book; his bubble reads “Skim’s summary · 1 of 5” over the section’s tldr. The section is the one at the reading line, a third of the way down the pane.

states.title: next section
states.description: The old line lifts out through a 4px blur (200ms) as the next rises in (360ms); the count moves on.

states.title: dizzy
states.description: Scrolling faster than 2.4px per ms, or Skip to the end: his eyes become spirals for about a second and he says “Whoa. Slow down, I’m reading.”

states.title: yawn
states.description: Four seconds without a scroll: he yawns for 2.2s (“Still on your data…”) and goes back to reading, then yawns again every six seconds you stay; any scroll wakes him.

states.title: read
states.description: The pane reaches its end: thumbs up, “That’s everything. Nothing sneaky.”, Skip to the end goes and Accept lights up.

states.title: accepted
states.description: Accept → Accepting → Accepted with a drawn check; “Thanks for reading. Well, skimming.” If onAccept throws, the button shakes into Try again.
